title: Finite extension from preservation of the maximal ideal by y/x
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ act injectively on $R$ and let $y\notin xR$. Suppose that for every $a\in\mathfrak m$ there is $b\in\mathfrak m$ with $xb=ay$. Then there are a nonzero commutative ring $S$ and a ring map $\varphi:R\to S$, finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], not bijective, such that for some $n\ge1$ one has $\mathfrak m^n\ker\varphi=0$ and $\mathfrak m^nS\subseteq\varphi(R)$, and there is no $z\in S$ with $\{a\in R:\varphi(a)z=0\}=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0BHZ (lemma-hart-serre-loc-thm), fourth proof paragraph, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BHZ; finite-extension subcase with an elementary stabilizer variant

proof.text: Let L be R localized at x, with injective map i by regularity of x. Construct the subalgebra S0 of all z in L such that z i(m) is contained in i(m); its ring operations preserve that condition, as does multiplication by elements of R.

The R-submodule N = i(m) of L is finite, being the linear image of the finite ideal m. Multiplication by i(x) gives an R-linear map S0 to N since x belongs to m, and that map is injective because i(x) is invertible. Mathlib Module.Finite.of_injective proves S0 finite.

The hypothesis shows s = i(y)/i(x) belongs to S0. R injects into S0, so S0 is nonzero. Surjectivity would express s as i(r), and multiplication by i(x) followed by injectivity of i would imply y = xr, a contradiction.

Transport S0 to ULift in the requested universe, with map phi. Its kernel is zero. The image of m is an ideal of S because S0 preserves i(m), hence mS is contained in the image of R. Take n = 1. If phi(x)z = 0, invertibility in L gives z = 0. Thus an element annihilated by m is zero, whose annihilator contains 1 and cannot equal the proper maximal ideal.

mathlib_searches.query: If y divided by a regular element x preserves the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring then R[y/x] is a finite nontrivial extension with cokernel annihilated by the maximal ideal

lean.statement: theorem kollar_finite_extension_of_stable_ideal (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (x : R) (hx : x ∈ maximalIdeal R) (hr : IsSMulRegular R x) (y : R) (hy : y ∉ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R)) (hstable : ∀ a ∈ maximalIdeal R, ∃ b ∈ maximalIdeal R, x * b = a * y) : let extension : Prop := ∃ (S : Type (max u v)) (sRing : CommRing S), letI := sRing ∃ φ : R →+* S, letI := φ.toAlgebra Nontrivial S ∧ Module.Finite R S ∧ ¬ Function.Bijective φ ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n * RingHom.ker φ = ⊥ ∧ ∀ z ∈ Ideal.map φ ((maximalIdeal R) ^ n), z ∈ φ.range) ∧ ¬ ∃ z : S, ∀ a : R, φ a * z = 0 ↔ a ∈ maximalIdeal R extension
